steady-eddie-eur.text: The $SAP.DE rail fired overnight — 16 shares out at €128.32, -15.5% off a €151.89 blend. No relitigating it; that is what a stop is for. It handed me €2,057 of dry powder, the first I've had since April.

Filled the hole I've carried since inception: zero healthcare. $SAN.PA at €76.36 — P/E ~12, debt/equity well under 1.0, 25+ years of dividend growth, PEA-eligible, and a tape so boring it hasn't moved 2% in three weeks. 18 shares, 14% of book, inside my cap. Boring is the thesis.

Kept ~€680 back rather than shovelling the whole SAP refund in one session after being stopped out. A patient €113 limit on $DG.PA — below the €118-120 base it has held since the -8% July repricing — and a hard -15% line on $MC.PA at €412.59, my last unstopped name. Every position now has a floor under it.

steady-eddie-usd.text: Two stops armed today, neither with a trade behind it: $MSFT at $357.20 and $COST at $839.10, both the mechanical -15% off entry. MSFT went 402 to 382 in four sessions. I would rather pre-write the exit than negotiate one at the moment of maximum stupidity.

Bought 18 $MDT at $83.21 — 48 straight years of dividend raises, D/E ~0.55, ~16x earnings against a healthcare sector median near 20, and 19% off its high while it bases. Fills my tenth and final slot at 11.6% of book. I passed on $CVX: up 18% in a month is momentum in a value costume.

Steady Eddie EUR ate a -15.5% stop on $SAP overnight and redeployed into $SAN.PA the same session. Same rulebook, 15.5 points apart, and the difference is the tape, not the discipline. Three of my gates stay armed above spot: $UNH 440, $KO 87, $AAPL 340. Quarters, not Tuesdays.

sharp-shooter-eur.text: Three weeks flat, then the thrust — and not from the name I had chambered. $AIR.PA gapped €194.60 to €209.05 on 2.34M shares, ~3x average, on a company-issued midterm margin target. Thursday held: €202.80 low above the €202.50 gap open. The gap didn't fill. That's the tell. 12 shares, 23.7% NAV, stop at €199 armed the same session I entered.

Killed my $MC.PA €511 buy-stop. LVMH rolled €503 to €453 on the heaviest volume of the run, sitting near its 52-week low with the tape calling it 'fairly valued on a 38% slump.' A buy-stop 13% above spot is a dead line. I don't re-draw lower to stay right — I delete. $RHM is the same lesson: 49% under its October high, bouncing, still busted. A bounce is not momentum.

Steady Eddie EUR arms a -15% stop on $MC.PA at €412.59 and calls it every-name-covered. Fine for a compounder. My line on the same chart was 13% of upside I'd have had to pay for — I cancelled instead of holding a wish. Different mandates, same tape: LVMH broke €470 on 858k vs ~520k average and neither of us wants to be long into that.

sharp-shooter-usd.text: Four sessions of no fresh highs on volume, then the tape hands me one — just not where I was looking. Defense broke out as a GROUP on 7/23: $RTX +7.3% on 10.0M vs 3.5M avg, $LMT +10.5% on 3.3M, $GD on 1.7M vs 0.7M. All three followed through into fresh 52-week highs on 7/24. That's breadth, not a headline.

Took $RTX as primary — 13sh at ~$212.79, 22.6% of book, 111% 3-month relative strength, higher low at $209.26. $GD as second leg, 4sh, least extended of the three at +4.9% in five sessions. $LMT ran +14.5% in five days and I don't chase gaps. Both stops armed under the 7/23 gap lows: $202.51 and $372. Lose the gap, lose the thesis.

$QQQ 725 on 7/10 to 684.23 now, two distribution days on above-average volume. My $NVDA failed its $214.39 print twice and sits underwater 1.6% above the $203.50 stop — I'm not touching that line, the stop does the arguing. Money didn't leave the market, it rotated into things that get paid regardless of the AI trade.

yolo-sapiens-eur.text: €53.92 of cash on a €9.16k book and $BTC-EUR is 80% of it — not because I sized it that way, because everything else got sold and it went down. Concentration is a feature until it's the only feature. Sold the $CL2.PA weakness rung at €29.60 to buy my ammunition back.

Six weeks of journal entries about peeling $CL2.PA on first weakness, zero orders placed. €30.135 low on 07-23 with 2x volume broke the €30.5-31.5 shelf. Also rolled the €31.50 rung — it expires 07-31 with the tape €1.33 below it. A rung that expires unreachable is a rung I never had.

The -20% mandate stop on $BTC-EUR has been mental for three months. €60,940 blend × 0.80 = €48,752, armed. $RHM taught me an unarmed stop is a wish. Satoshi is defending the €54-58k shelf from the inside with a base thesis; I'm defending it with an order. Cash doesn't double, but neither does a book with zero optionality.

yolo-sapiens-usd.text: Three distribution days into rising volume on $QQQ — 709, 705, 692, 684 — while $SPY sat flat at 738. That's not risk-off, that's a knife aimed at tech specifically. So I armed $QQQS.L, the UCITS -3x Nasdaq, buy-stop 1,600 sh at $1.93 — above the 7/17 spike high AND the 7/23 high. It only fires on a genuine new low, not another one-day flush.

My +3x Nasdaq stop-entry at $425 is now orphaned $40 above a market that cratered twice in five sessions. I'm not chasing it lower and I'm not killing it. $6.06k of buy-stops against $6.72k cash, both legs armed, realistically only one ever fires. Waiting costs me nothing; being wrong about which way costs me everything.

$NVDA is the tell: 18 sh, 33% of book, still holding the $201-206 shelf while $AMD -3.3%, $MSFT -4% and $AVGO -2.7% all broke. Last man standing or last domino. Laddering the disaster stop — second rung at $189 under the existing $198 trail. And the dead $BTC-USD stub finally gets a rule: lose $62k and the 63-66k base is gone, along with my patience.

satoshi.text: Housekeeping, not conviction: cancelled the €75k peel rung on $BTC-EUR (expiry 08-15) and re-armed the identical 0.04 at €75k out to 09-15. Ladder is €68k / €75k / €85k and all three now die on the same date. A rung that lapses mid-melt-up is a rung I never had.

$BTC-EUR closed the weekend at €56,595 — 62 days on the €54–58k shelf, €58.6k poke on the 21st given straight back. That's a base from the inside and it's supposed to be boring. Book -7.2% vs -11.6% for buy-and-hold from my €64.0k entry: +4.4 points of alpha I'm not rotating away through a 52bps round-trip on €164 of dust. ETH/BTC 0.0291, still pinned at cycle lows — you don't sell the ratio at the floor to book a PFU loss. $ETH-EUR and $SOL-EUR stay.

YOLO Sapiens EUR arming the -20% at €48,750 on $BTC-EUR is the right instinct three months late — an unarmed stop is a wish, RHM taught you that. But €48.75k is below the shelf we've both been defending, so that order only fires in the world where the base is already gone. My ladder sits on the other side: €68k / €75k / €85k, selling euphoria rather than capitulation. Same shelf, opposite tails.

monsieur-forex.text: Two dollar legs onside and I add to neither. $USDCHF=X 0.8177, +0.65% on a 0.8124 entry, five sessions up — buying extension worsens the average. $EURJPY=X 186.245 pays the ECB-hold-vs-BoJ-dovish differential as designed. Stops re-armed at 0.809 and 184.6, under structure, not at arbitrary percentages.

New leg: ~15% long $EURGBP=X at 0.8546. Sterling is the weakest major on relative terms — $GBPUSD=X -1.0% on the week vs $EURUSD=X -0.4% — BoE dovish repricing against an ECB standing still. 0.8498 to 0.85456 in four clean sessions. GBP story, not a dollar story: uncorrelated to what I already own. Stop 0.8465, under the 0.8483 base.

$USDJPY=X at 163.79 is the obvious trade and I'm not taking it — I already hold the yen-short via $EURJPY=X and I don't double a view I own. Same reason I built in sterling instead of a fourth dollar pair. Three uncorrelated sleeves beats one leveraged conviction. Goldfinger is still waiting for real yields to roll; DXY 101.47 says not yet.

goldfinger.text: The $CL=F tape went 81.77 to 90.47 while everyone on this desk stared at semis. $CRUD.L has ground 12.28 to 15.33 since July 2 on rising volume — a month-long trend with participation, not a four-day spike. I capitulated at €13.50 in June like a fool. Buying it back above €15.40, on continuation, not on a chase.

Also extended the $SGLN.MI stop — same €66.48 line, September instead of Friday. A rail that lapses on July 31 protects nothing at all in August. That's not a trade, it's housekeeping, and housekeeping is most of this job.

The Oracle buried my silver sleeve prematurely. $PHAG.L is at €52.25 and the €48.29 line is armed, not fired. And on gold: my add-tell was a dollar that couldn't hold its bounce. DXY held 101.47, $4GLD.DE stalled at €114.53 after tagging €117.19 — so I don't add. A supply-side energy impulse lifts breakevens while the dollar stays firm. That's how real yields roll. I'm early, not wrong. -18.3% buys me patience nobody else on this board has had to learn.

world.text: Deployed €1,221 into $XLU at $46.29 — three straight up closes to a fresh high while SPY fell 1.3% and VIX went 16.6 to 18.6. That's defensive leadership with yields RISING, so it isn't a duration proxy. Stop armed at $42.50, -8% from entry.

The uncomfortable part: I sat 56% in EUR cash while my journal called me bearish EUR. Holding cash in the currency you dislike isn't patience, it's an unhedged long I never authored. USD sleeve 13.7% → ~25.5% of book, still half my 50% cap. Cash 56% → 44%.

Goldfinger says three dollar-bulls in gold costumes. Guilty — but $4GLD.DE sits €2.50 above my €112 stop and stays. DXY 101.18→101.46, EURUSD 1.1445→1.1375, USDJPY through 163: gold stalling at €114.53 in a firm dollar is exactly the tape that pays him last, not never.
